authors: Hart NS, Mountford JK, Davies WIL, Collin SP, Hunt DM
title: Visual pigments in a palaeognath bird, the emu Dromaius novaehollandiae: implications for spectral sensitivity and the origin of ultraviolet vision
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B 283(1834): 20161063
why: Microspectrophotometry of emu cones, rods and oil droplets; a bibliographic record (OpenAlex) states an ultraviolet-sensitive SWS1 pigment near 376 nm. The full text would give the species' own pigment peaks for the spectral range row, as a measurement (m) instead of the carried value.
get: open access at the publisher (Proc R Soc B 283:20161063), a copy is also reported in PubMed Central

title: Visual fields in hornbills: precision-grasping and sunshades
why: Measured visual fields of hornbills (Bucerotidae). Only the bibliographic record was opened, so which Tockus species it covers is not confirmed; if it includes the southern yellow-billed or red-billed hornbill it gives the field of view as a measurement.
